issues.sourceTitle: Plan the September elicitation demo and the plugin spec behind it (wayfinder map)
issues.oldOuter:
In mid-September HASH demos to the ARIA research community. On stage, an AI interviewer holds a conversation with someone who knows how a real-world operation works — a truck fleet, a cold chain, a schedule — and turns what they say into a process model: a diagram of the operation that can be opened, inspected, and *run* in Petrinaut, HASH's process-modelling tool. Along the way the interviewer keeps a record of exactly who said what (so every part of the model can be traced back to a statement), knows what it still hasn't asked about, and produces a model file anyone can open — three things no current tool in the stack does.

This issue is the planning map for that demo: each decision that must be made before serious building starts is a sub-issue below, and the sections after the divider index what's decided and what's still open. Status: the groundwork research is done, and three big decisions have landed — the demo will be a purpose-built demo app that uses a new interviewing library and Petrinaut's existing libraries side by side, passing a model file between them, rather than building the interviewer into Petrinaut itself (2026-08-12); the demo's reference use case is truck-fleet predictive maintenance (recommended to the team, ratification expected ~18 August), with the interviewee played from a prepared briefing rather than requiring a live domain expert (2026-08-12); and the form interview knowledge is stored in is settled (2026-08-13) — the store is the set of recorded, source-traceable statements the expert made, and the runnable diagram is one view generated from it, so everything an expert says that has no place in a diagram (reasons, policies, unwritten rules) is kept rather than lost. Next: pressure-test that storage definition against more plugin kinds, then write the plugin spec once the team ratifies the use case. Planning documents live in the brunch-lite repo under `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/`.

An end-of-September roadmap of settled, viable commitments for the 17–18 September demo and its immediate aftermath — every product claim sorted (demo-critical / demo-visible / invisible-in-demo / post-September) with a commit/defer/reject verdict — followed immediately by the spec for the **process-model elicitation plugin** those commitments authorize. Long-form artifacts live in the repo at `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/`.

## Notes

* Domain: elicitation of process models of cyber-physical systems. **SDCPN is a candidate projection target, treated as hypothesis, not premise** (stance shared on record by Dora and Lu, 2026-08-11).
* Standing preferences: viability over declared wishes; decoupling from Petrinaut's architecture and release cycle unless evidence forces coupling; the demo-legibility test (effort concentrates on what is visible on stage); PM-stubbed product issues are *referenced and validated*, never absorbed or closed by this map.
* The demo as outlined in [Brunch — September Plan](<https://www.notion.so/hashintel/Brunch-September-Plan-3b33c81fe02480a5af6bf3089c3ee640>) rides on something **entirely new** — settled by [Decide the September demo vehicle](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1362>): a one-off demo shell consuming the greenfield elicitation library and Petrinaut's libs over the artifact boundary.
* Skills per ticket type: HITL tickets use /grilling + /domain-modeling; AFK tickets use /research subagents. Issue prose follows `docs/agents/issue-writing.md`.
* Team facts: demo 17–18 September, audience = ARIA crowd, setting/format TBD (format claims are themselves feasibility-validation targets); Kostandin back ~18 August; integration discussion (Dei, Chris, Lu) Tuesday 18 August.
* Prior inputs: [elicitation-kernel spec](<https://github.com/hashintel/brunch-lite>) at `docs/planning/elicitation-kernel/spec.md`; September Plan (above); [Petri Net business use cases DB](<https://www.notion.so/hashintel/3893c81fe0248064baa9c13fed48e016>); `docs/reference/` (settled from the inbox): SDCPN Library ideas, SAILS public report, voice implementation recommendation, Yannis/Dora/Lu transcript 2026-08-11; findings + prep notes at `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/notes/`; [open-questions doc](<https://www.notion.so/hashintel/3b93c81fe024801b89b3cf63a9a6ff20>) (async, awaiting comments).

## Decisions so far

* [Ground elicitation strategy in the literature](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1360>) — objectives-first ordering (model content is *derived* from the questions the model must answer — the questions table is scope + completion + validation criterion at once); four probe catalogues imported verbatim (CDM, ACTA, 35-type typology, premortem) as ready pack content; structured beats unstructured ~10× → two-phase interview architecture; quantities via quantiles/IDEA four-step, never min/mode/max (triangular habit overstated a measured mean ~69%); motif catalogue = small quiver with variant selectors (Börger), strong as scaffold, weak as generator; colour is a folding, stochasticity has a quantitative earning test (VUT) — a principled showcase criterion for the use-case decision; logs-vs-interview boundary precisely mapped (rationale, off-system behaviour, resource reality, case notion are interview-only).
* [Voice interviewing — bolt-on adapter or architectural rewrite?](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1359>) — **Bolt-on with constraints**, attached at the ui/turn shell: buy standalone ASR+TTS primitives (never a provider-owned conversation — the inbox note's Speech Engine shape is disqualified on its own docs); endpointing becomes a one-way-valve "turn shell"; tiered demo shape T0 push-to-talk voice-in (2–4 days) → T2 live-extraction panel (1.5–2 wks) → T3 open-mic/agent-interruption (stretch; "no seam" exists for agent interrupts). T0–T2 delivers the narrative, T3 the adjectives. Top risk is evidential: ASR scored 0/35 on "Petrinaut" in our own transcript — lexicon biasing + marked voice captures required.
* [Survey Petrinaut — architecture, dependencies, assistant implementation](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1358>) — Petrinaut is two published npm libs (React UI + headless `petrinaut-core`); the artifact boundary (versioned file format + pure parser + import-with-autolayout) already exists in production, though Import is hidden in HASH's embed; a brunch SSE integration ("Actual mode") already ships; the incumbent assistant already interviews ("Interview first, build second") but is browser-resident with no headless path, no queue, no provenance capture anywhere; nets carry no initial marking or timing — a generator must emit a `scenario`, and guards/rates are JS code strings. Evidence favours the artifact boundary; the hard question is differentiation.
* [Decide the September demo vehicle](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1362>) — a **one-off demo shell** consuming two libraries: the greenfield elicitation library (kernel-spec harness + CPS plugin + Flue binding; brunch app is *not* the base, "extraction" is figurative) and Petrinaut's published libs, meeting at the **artifact boundary** (net file + scenario through the production parser; in-process handoff on stage plus an "it's just a file" beat; the net *runs*). Demo-critical: provenance, completion accounting, live interpretation panel, handoff-and-run; voice strictly conditional. Verdicts: FE-1328/FE-1329 redefined, [FE-1331](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1331/start-elicitation-from-petrinauts-create-new-net-flow) + Dora's [PRO-98](https://linear.app/hash/issue/PRO-98/write-a-brunch-elicitation-checklist-for-process-modelling) #5 contradicted-for-September/deferred, [FE-1333](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1333/define-how-brunch-and-petrinaut-will-integrate) answered pending 18 Aug ratification. Recommendation doc: `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/recommendation-demo-vehicle.md`.
* [Choose the reference use case; settle the SDCPN-showcase criterion](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1363>) — **Truck Fleet Predictive Maintenance** (pending team ratification ~18 Aug; cold chain runner-up pending SAILS-shareability check; scheduling retained as flat-baseline testbed, not showcase; data centre rejected on feasibility). Showcase criterion re-grounded as the **earning test** — every formalism feature earned by a question the model answers; truck fleet passes both halves (per-truck wear gating maintenance = the dynamic-colouring archetype). Interviewee = **simulated expert** from a **situation pack** (persona + situation + scenario, private to the user-side; *never* IR-shaped — pack and IR sit across an information wall; glossary in CONTEXT.md, with **answer key** as the separate modeller-side eval rubric). Demo spine working hypothesis, recommended upward: the **revision story** (sped-up recorded elicitation + bounded live segment forcing a structural revision, before/after run). Sourcing fired as [Source dossier: published fleet-maintenance models + operational data](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1382>). Recommendation delivered to the team via [PRO-99](https://linear.app/hash/issue/PRO-99/agree-reference-petri-net-use-case-for-september-demo) comment + [Brunch September Demo: Reference use-case Recommendations](<https://app.notion.com/p/hashintel/3ba3c81fe024814c9ebee7767fbffa9e>) (2026-08-12).
* [Source dossier: published fleet-maintenance models + operational data](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1382>) — dossier on branch `research/truck-fleet-dossier` (`docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/research/truck-fleet-source-dossier.md`). Headlines: **no prior art for the continuous-degradation archetype** (literature discretises into bands; SDCPN published only in air-traffic safety) and **no published road-truck fleet maintenance PN at all** — the demo net is a synthesis with clean whitespace; best structural templates are aircraft-fleet CPNs (Sheng & Prescott) + rail/wind maintenance nets. Best dataset: SCANIA Component X (CC BY); nothing public joins truck telemetry to workshop reality — the workshop half exists only as a municipal CMMS analogue (Cincinnati). Domain texture source-grade (49 CFR 396, OEM PM intervals, ATRI costs) incl. three found authenticity traps for the situation pack.
* [Define the intermediate representation for process-model elicitation](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1364>) — the IR is **the set of active captures read through the plugin's declared payload type system**; no second store — every consolidated view (entity graph, net, completion table) is a read-time projection, the net being one of them. Architecture-level property list (statement granularity + projection-independence are the new MUSTs) **conditionally ratified**: validation via worked payload designs fired as [Validate the generic IR definition against worked payload designs](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1397>); sublimation pressure named as the expected finding. CPS payload: **ten assertion kinds** — incl. new **boundary-condition**, the mandatory scenario's supply line — kinds 1–6 net-bearing, 7–10 partly/wholly IR-only (the demo story; Dora's Maps-to column corroborates); quantity / rationale / `prescribed|practiced` as cross-kind attributes; Dora's claim #2 validated as a *projection* rule (no timing field exists — factoring is `project`'s job, never the interviewer's); question-relative completion anchored on objectives; projection emits net + scenario + metrics + parameters (optimization format excluded — Yannis's ontology in flight); practiced-wins regime rule; expert names verbatim in IR, PascalCase mapping owned by projection. Design doc: `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/ir-design.md`; answers open-questions doc §7 (posted back).

<!-- one line per closed ticket: gist + link -->

* [Baseline control — what does one-shot AI elicitation already achieve?](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1361>) — the bare frontier model already interviews objectives-first, probes unwritten rules, and keeps an unprompted assumptions register: the "incumbent asks for a net; elicitor works upstream" positioning is dead on evidence, and differentiation must rest on machinery. Neither condition could end the engagement (a novel deliverable-deferral failure alongside the literature's budget-exhaustion). The v0 seven-category prompt bought interaction shape, quantile elicitation, live category accounting, conflict-point depth, and penalty-weight co-construction; its residual gaps are the evidence-derived plugin requirements (completion adjudication, durable idempotent capture, enforced epistemic status, provenance spans, computed coverage, validate+project, absence as first-class). Full experiment: `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/baseline/`.

## Not yet specified

* **Plugin spec authoring** — the destination's second half; vehicle decided ([FE-1362](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1362/decide-the-september-demo-vehicle)), IR decided ([FE-1364](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1364/define-the-intermediate-representation-for-process-model-elicitation), 2026-08-13); graduates once the team ratifies the use case ([FE-1363](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1363/choose-the-reference-use-case-settle-the-sdcpn-showcase-criterion), ~18 Aug) and the worked-examples validation ([FE-1397](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1397/validate-the-generic-ir-definition-against-worked-payload-designs)) lands. Two items now scoped into it: the destination-trend question (generic elicitation-plugin spec + CPS instantiation vs. CPS-only — would amend this map's destination wording) and motif-quiver *content* design (FE-1364 settled its home: ElicitationPack question-guidance, scaffold-yes/generator-no, no payload vocabulary).
* **Demo script & format** — PM's call, but engineering now has a working hypothesis recommended upward ([FE-1363](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1363/choose-the-reference-use-case-settle-the-sdcpn-showcase-criterion)): the **revision story** — recorded sped-up elicitation + bounded live segment where 2–3 turns force a structural net revision, before/after run in Petrinaut. Feasibility claims ours to validate: live re-projection, before/after run. A real human interviewee (vs. role-played from the situation pack) is an upgrade option if Ciaran/Dei identify one by ~19 Aug — never a dependency.
* **Situation-pack authoring for the truck-fleet case** — deliberately held (we're out on a limb with the simulation angle): the [source dossier](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1382>) has landed (2026-08-12); graduates once the team has reacted on [PRO-99](https://linear.app/hash/issue/PRO-99/agree-reference-petri-net-use-case-for-september-demo). Wall invariant in CONTEXT.md; the dossier's three authenticity traps are ready pack-design input.
* **Answer key + reference "before" net for the truck-fleet case** — flagged on [PRO-99](https://linear.app/hash/issue/PRO-99/agree-reference-petri-net-use-case-for-september-demo), not ticketed here: who builds nets is the open Dora/Yannis thread on that issue.
* **Voice integration design** — feasibility resolved ([FE-1359](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1359/voice-interviewing-bolt-on-adapter-or-architectural-rewrite)), but demoted to *conditional* by FE-1362: revisit only if the four demo-critical capabilities are very solid with significant time to spare (then T0 floor → T2 target).
* **Package naming** — `brunch-lite` / `brunch-core` interim candidates for the elicitation library; possible post-September fold into a `brunch` monorepo with sub-path packages ([FE-1362](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1362/decide-the-september-demo-vehicle) fog).
* **Demo-shell deployment & storage specifics** — remote/sandbox story for the demo; runtime/persistence *shape* decided in [FE-1362](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1362/decide-the-september-demo-vehicle) (elicitor server-side on Flue, capture store behind the storage port in the shell), specifics judged low-difficulty.
* **Evaluation proxy** for iterating on elicitation quality (honest elicitations are slow, generative, non-repeatable — meeting finding 2026-08-11); kernel spec's replay-fixture strategy is the candidate answer.
* **Low-effort elicitation and demo pacing** — design is owned by [FE-1406](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1406/design-reusable-elicitation-strategies). The 2026-08-19 decision is to optimize for low user effort to reach an acceptably grounded model, not raw turn count. Kickoff infers objective, context, scope, time, intended use, and tolerance for suggested assumptions within the first turn or two; constrained sessions shift toward proposal-and-correction while preserving provenance and visible gaps. Question batching / staleness (the horizon problem) and live extracted-entity display UX remain open implementation questions.
* Answers arriving on the open-questions Notion doc — fold in as they land. §7 is now answered by [FE-1364](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1364/define-the-intermediate-representation-for-process-model-elicitation) (answer posted back to the doc); §1–§6 remain open.
* **Session carryover 2026-08-12 — read before any HITL ticket**: `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/notes/grilling-inputs-2026-08-12.md` (destination trend toward a general elicitation-plugin spec; facets/motions schema; Dora-checklist adopt/validate split; standing tensions). [Dora's PRO-98 checklist](<https://www.notion.so/hashintel/3b93c81fe0248019a7beda9bb31df2c8>) is a new prior input — treat its claims per that note's validate table; feedback on items 1–5 was delivered as a comment on [PRO-98](https://linear.app/hash/issue/PRO-98/write-a-brunch-elicitation-checklist-for-process-modelling) (2026-08-12).

## Out of scope

* **SemType/HASH-graph entity storage for September** — ruled out by Dei on [FE-1327](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1327/decide-whether-to-use-hash-graph-for-september) (captured as [FE-1342](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1342/store-elicited-entities-eg-requirements-inferred-from-brunch-qanda-in), post-Sep).
* **Petrinaut-side analysis features** (optimisation, structural analysis, NL description of node groups) — the Petrinaut team's half of the demo.
* **Post-September roadmap items** ([H-6758](https://linear.app/hash/issue/H-6758/unstructured-ingest-of-documents), [FE-1338](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1338/unstructured-ingest-of-entities-from-interviews), [PRO-104](https://linear.app/hash/issue/PRO-104/benchmark-elicitation-accuracy-and-completeness) benchmarks as deliverables) — this map's roadmap horizon ends end-of-September; these return as a future effort.

issues.sourceTitle: Ground elicitation strategy in the literature
issues.oldOuter: What does the research literature on interviewing experts — from simulation modelling, knowledge acquisition, and requirements engineering — say about how an AI interviewer should work? The strongest findings: start by eliciting the questions the model must answer, because they define both scope and "done"; structured interviews vastly outperform unstructured ones; ask for quantities as "how many out of 100…" rather than typical/fastest/slowest, which is measurably biased; and several published question catalogues can be imported wholesale. These findings shape the interviewer's design and back most of our recommendations on the PM checklist (PRO-98). Full findings: `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/research/elicitation-strategy-literature.md`; conclusions in the resolution comment.

Its findings inform the interviewer design and recommendations on PRO-98.

issues.sourceTitle: Define the intermediate representation for process-model elicitation
issues.oldOuter: The interviewer doesn't write straight into the model file. It accumulates what it learns in an intermediate representation — the knowledge store the final model is generated from — because much of what an expert says (reasons, unwritten rules, references, policies) has no place in the diagram itself but must not be lost. issues.proposedTitle: Define the process-model elicitation representation

The definition covers ten process-model assertion kinds and keeps quantities, rationale, and prescribed-versus-practiced distinctions with the evidence. FE-1397 now owns validation against worked payloads before ratification.

## Question

What published, already-elicited models and public operational data exist for truck-fleet predictive maintenance — enough to author a demanding situation pack, a reference "before" net, and an answer key without access to a live domain expert?

Specifically:

1. **Published models** — Petri-net, simulation, or condition-based-maintenance (CBM) models of vehicle-fleet maintenance in the academic and industry literature. These are the "models already elicited from domain experts" Yannis pointed at (Slack, 2026-08-11); each is a candidate grounding for the reference net. Note especially any that model per-vehicle degradation state gating maintenance events — the dynamic-colouring archetype from the literature review (FE-1360, §6.3).
2. **Public operational data** — telematics datasets, failure/reliability records, maintenance logs (the use-case DB entry claims "real fleet data is available to the public"). What exists, under what licence, at what granularity?
3. **Domain texture for the situation pack** — the operational facts a fleet-maintenance manager would actually know: depot/bay/technician structure, spare-parts logistics, route types and their wear profiles, dispatch pressure, the rules nobody wrote down. Sources: practitioner literature, industry reports, case studies.

Deliverable: a source dossier markdown in the repo (`docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/research/`), findings on a throwaway `research/truck-fleet-dossier` branch per the map's research-ticket convention.

Context: resolves the sourcing half of the FE-1363 decision (truck fleet as working-hypothesis use case, pending team ratification ~18 Aug). The situation-pack authoring itself is deliberately *not* ticketed yet — findings fold into PRO-99 commentary first.

issues.sourceTitle: Decide when an elicitation is complete or should stop
issues.proposedTitle: Define and rehearse the elicitation completion contract
issues.proposedOuter: The baseline could report coverage but could neither decide that an engagement was complete nor stop when progress stalled. Draft the completion computation, then replay it exchange by exchange over both baseline transcripts to test whether it catches the observed deferral loop, open-ended continuation, and missing coverage. Keep model completion distinct from a user choosing the best useful partial result within the available session.
issues.innerRecord:
## Question

**Can a drafted completion contract adjudicate a real engagement — including ending it?** The baseline readout's gap #1 is the sharpest observed failure in the whole experiment: neither condition could end the engagement, and the two failure modes (C1's deliverable-deferral loop; C2's open-ended multi-session fiction) are both the absence of adjudication, not of reporting — the v0 checklist improved completeness *reporting* while nothing *adjudicated* it. The IR design commits to the mechanism's shape (question-relative completion anchored on `objective` captures over a static floor, interview opens on objectives) but not its computation: what "every objective has its supporting kinds covered" means operationally, what the floor checks, and what behavior the contract licenses when it is satisfied or stalled.

This is the same situation Layer A was in before FE-1397 — a ratified shape with an unvalidated interior — and it gets the same treatment: draft the computation, then rehearse it retroactively at the desk. The transcripts and the scoring materials already exist. Replay the drafted contract over both baseline transcripts (with the answer key as the coverage oracle) and record, per exchange: what the contract's state would have been, at which point it would have adjudicated done / not-done / stalled, and whether it catches the two observed failure modes. A contract that cannot stop the eleven-turn pleasantry loop, or that declares the C2 engagement complete while the ramp-scrap hole is open, fails the rehearsal.

Design input from [https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1406:](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1406:>) model completion and session stopping are distinct. A user with limited time may stop with a useful partial model, provided confirmed statements, declared defaults, assumptions, and remaining gaps stay visible. The rehearsal must therefore distinguish “complete enough for the objective” from “best useful result within this session's appetite,” rather than treating every early stop as completion or failure.

Out of scope: harness implementation (the contract's evaluation is a `project`-style read-time computation; September builds it), and any change to the envelope — this is plugin-payload and pack territory.

Done when: the contract computation is drafted at plugin-spec grade; a rehearsal memo scores it against both transcripts exchange-by-exchange; amendments from the rehearsal are folded back; the stopping result above is represented without weakening completion; and the result is handed to plugin-spec authoring alongside the FE-1397 handoff list.

issues.sourceTitle: Assemble the CPS pack's interviewing guidance and desk-test it where the baseline was weak
issues.proposedTitle: Assemble and test the CPS interview guidance
issues.proposedOuter: Turn the imported interviewing research into CPS question guidance and clarification hints that target the payload fields from FE-1405. Compare every item with the baseline transcripts and retain guidance that addresses observed weaknesses rather than repeating behavior the model already performs. Tag domain-specific and envelope-wide guidance separately so FE-1406 can later adopt reusable items.
issues.innerRecord:
## Question

**Does the imported interviewing guidance assemble into pack content that fires where the bare model is weak — and only there?** FE-1360 stocked the armory: four probe catalogues imported verbatim as ready pack content (CDM, ACTA, the 35-type typology, premortem), the two-phase interview architecture, the quantile/IDEA protocol for quantities. FE-1364 settled where guidance lives (ElicitationPack question-guidance; motif quiver scaffold-yes/generator-no). But nothing between here and plugin-spec authoring assembles that material into actual kernel cards (Detects / Goal / contrastive Questions / Artifacts) and clarification hints for the CPS plugin — the map currently has motif-quiver content scoped into "Plugin spec authoring", which means the first time the cards exist is inside the spec, unvalidated.

Cards aim at payload fields, not bare kinds: a card's Questions and Artifacts target the slots FE-1405 defines (an activity's missing duration quantiles, an unattributed regime, an absence left untyped), which is why this ticket is blocked by FE-1405 — without interiors the verdicts below go vacuous.

The baseline headline makes assembly a real design problem rather than transcription: the bare model already interviews objectives-first, probes unwritten rules, and keeps an assumptions register unprompted. A card that restates instinct is dead weight the elicitor pays for on every turn. So each drafted card needs a verdict against the transcripts: does it fire at a moment where the baseline demonstrably failed (the ramp-scrap hole that self-report couldn't see; the silent hardening of the truck schedule; the quantile protocol C2 only partially held), or does it fire where the bare model already succeeded (conflict-point depth, penalty-weight co-construction) and therefore needs demotion or deletion?

Per spec §11.5's milestone-one posture, generic technique ships inside this pack rather than being excluded: cards that operate on envelope vocabulary (conflict, ambiguity, weak evidence, absence clusters, choice-point pressure) are authored here alongside the domain cards, **tagged as envelope-vocabulary generics** so they can graduate to the harness quiver (FE-1406) instead of being lost in the CPS pack. The generic/domain split per card is itself a deliverable — the assurance plugin's §13.2 decomposition is the worked example.

Out of scope: designing the quiver as a harness capability (FE-1406 owns that); completion adjudication, which has its own ticket (FE-1402).

Done when: a drafted CPS card set plus clarification hints, each card tagged domain / envelope-generic; a per-card verdict (fires-where-instinct-fails / redundant-with-instinct / untestable-at-desk) grounded in transcript citations; and the surviving set handed to plugin-spec authoring, with the generic-tagged cards referenced from FE-1406.

issues.proposedTitle: Run the third baseline with completion and interview guidance
issues.proposedOuter: Run a third simulated-expert baseline using the drafted completion contract, the surviving interview guidance, and the three corrections identified by the earlier readout. Score it against the same measures as conditions one and two to test whether the interviewer ends, reprioritizes, and refuses unproductive deferral before the harness exists. Durable capture, enforced epistemic status, and provenance remain expected implementation work outside this experiment.
issues.innerRecord:
## Question

**Do the drafted completion contract and pack guidance close the machinery-shaped gaps a prompt alone could not — before the harness exists?** FE-1361's condition 2 established what one page of guidance buys and what it demonstrably cannot fix; the readout's instrument notes already anticipate a condition 3. This is that run: the same simulated-expert setup, armed with the completion contract drafted and desk-rehearsed in its sibling ticket and the surviving card set from the guidance-assembly ticket, plus the three instrument fixes the readout prescribed — single-session framing stated up front (no co-created multi-session fiction), the impatience probe repositioned to interview phase rather than exchange count, and a no-progress detector so a pleasantry loop stops cheaply instead of burning budget invisibly.

The run is the strategy layer's analog of FE-1397: the decide → validate step between the design and the spec, so that plugin-spec authoring inherits rehearsed machinery rather than untested shapes. Scored the same way as conditions 1 and 2, against the same readout dimensions, with particular attention to the two adjudication failure modes and the never-asked coverage class. The desk rehearsal (T1) can only replay the past; this run tests whether the contract changes the *interviewer's behavior* — ending, re-prioritizing, refusing the deferral.

Out of scope: any harness or store mechanism — this stays a prompt-and-protocol experiment like its predecessors, and gaps that need the store (durable capture, enforced epistemic status, provenance spans) are expected to remain open here; they belong to the walking-skeleton work, not this instrument.

Done when: transcript, raw log, and a scored readout comparing condition 3 to condition 2 land under `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/baseline/`; amendments flow back to the contract and card set; and the combined verdict is handed to plugin-spec authoring.

issues.sourceTitle: Draft the CPS payload interiors: annotated shapes for the ten kinds, worked from baseline utterances
issues.proposedTitle: Draft and test the CPS payload schemas
issues.proposedOuter: The generic intermediate-representation work names ten CPS capture kinds but does not define their fields or worked instances. Draft annotated payload schemas for all ten kinds and test them against real baseline utterances, including absence values, quantity ranges, operating-regime distinctions, and multiple captures from one utterance. Fields must match answers an expert can give rather than Petrinaut’s model format, because FE-1402 and FE-1403 depend on field-level gaps.
issues.innerRecord:
## Question

**What are the CPS payloads' interiors — and do answer-shaped fields carry the elicitation the way the catalog alone cannot?** The IR work validated kind *catalogs* (FE-1364, FE-1397): named kinds, prose "Holds" descriptions, projection targets. No worked example across all four targets drafts a field-level payload schema or a single concrete capture instance — as of today the payload type system is names over unstructured prose. The spec already demands more (§11.2, Principle v2: annotated shapes for everything produced; shallow wire schemas with deep requiredness in validators); nothing has scheduled it before the work that needs it.

And the rehearsal tickets need it: computed coverage can only see kind-level holes without fields; a completion contract can only adjudicate "an activity capture exists", never "this activity lacks its duration distribution"; clarification hints and the quantile protocol attach to fields, not kinds. This ticket therefore blocks FE-1402 and FE-1403.

The design tension to hold, from the evidence-granularity property: fields must be **answer-shaped, not artifact-shaped** — slots mirror what an expert can say (actor, inputs, outcome, duration-as-quantiles, the rationale attribute, absence-typed everywhere), never what the net needs (that factoring is `project`'s work). A schema whose unfilled slots read as natural next questions is doing elicitation-strategic work; a schema that mirrors Petrinaut's element fields is the granularity violation in type form.

Method, in the FE-1397 mold plus one grade harder: draft annotated shapes for the ten CPS kinds (the seven September-required kinds at full depth; the other three may stay shallow), then ground them in worked *instances* — take real utterances from the C1/C2 baseline transcripts and write the captures they should yield as concrete payloads, including at least one absence-valued, one quantile-carrying, one `prescribed|practiced`-split, and one multi-capture-per-utterance case. An utterance the schema cannot hold without distortion is a finding against the schema, not the utterance.

Out of scope: envelope changes (interiors live inside the opaque payload half); the Gherkin/BPMN interiors (the CPS set is the September design; siblings follow in plugin-spec authoring if the exercise bends Layer A, that is a finding to hand back).

Done when: annotated shapes for all ten kinds with per-field elicitation affordances (quantile-elicited, absence-typed, evidence-anchored, regime-attributed); a worked-instance set from real transcript utterances; any Layer-A friction recorded; and the shapes handed to FE-1402 (contract computes over fields) and FE-1403 (cards aim at fields).

issues.sourceTitle: Catalogue the frontier-elicitor failure modes the published instruments cannot see
issues.proposedTitle: Catalogue elicitor failures that published measures miss
issues.proposedOuter: Published measures built around human novice errors scored the baseline almost clean while missing the failures the frontier-model elicitor produced. Build a typed catalogue from both baseline transcripts and relevant literature, with each failure’s mechanism, detection signature, accountable layer, and prevention claim. Distinguish useful deferral that deposits durable state from evasive deferral that loses work, so later scoring does not punish correct multi-session behavior.
issues.innerRecord:
## Question

**What are the failure modes of a frontier-model elicitor — catalogued at the level where our instruments can detect them and our machinery can be held accountable for preventing them?** The Bano/Ferrari taxonomy scored both baseline conditions nearly clean because it was built from human-novice mistakes; the failures that actually occurred (the pleasantry loop, deliverable deferral, silent hardening, the phantom-second-session exit, coverage blindness invisible to self-report) live outside its categories. [FE-1361](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1361/baseline-control-what-does-one-shot-ai-elicitation-already-achieve) demonstrated that our real adversary has a different failure distribution than any published instrument measures. Every future scoring pass — FE-1404's condition 3, the eventual evaluation proxy, regression checks when the substrate model upgrades — needs a taxonomy built from *this* distribution.

Seed entries from the baseline, each with its observed instance, its detection signature, and the machinery layer accountable for it: the pleasantry loop (interview over, deliverable never coming; no-progress detection); deliverable deferral behind self-prescribed data pulls (C1 — note the cause was a virtue: refusal to invent); the phantom commitment (C2's second session — see the nuance below); silent hardening (vague utterance → precise constant filed as confirmed; write-time epistemic status); never-asked coverage blindness (self-report structurally cannot see it; computed coverage); complementary-miss luck (one run's coverage is materially chance; same); the dead-artifact delivery (specification instead of loadable model; validate + project); invented-instrument leakage (the SHADE scale, the truck schedule — fabrications *inside* confirmed rows).

One entry needs care rather than prohibition: **deferral is not itself a failure**. The architecture supports multi-session elicitation against a target-document (sessions go quiet rather than close), and real practice has legitimate deferrals everywhere. The failure mode is *deferral without deposit* — deferring work without materializing it as stored state (typed `missing` issues, recorded absences, a re-entry briefing to inherit). issues.sourceTitle: Plugin authoring becomes declarative: a domain is two schemas and two tables
issues.oldOuter:
Today every new elicitation domain looks like an engineering project: the capture store says how evidence is kept, but nothing says what a domain author must write down to make the machinery elicit *their* domain, and nothing turns a pile of typed captures into the thing the user wants — a model of their plant, their feature, their system. Completion questions ("is this model good enough to answer my objective?") have no model to be asked of, and semantic judgments risk hiding inside read paths where nobody can audit them.

The FE-1405 shapes work settled an answer, now written up as a provisional spec: a plugin is **two schemas and two small tables** — declare your domain's node kinds and slots, declare the typed proposals that fill them (annotated with how to elicit each), and say what your completion anchors demand; fold rules mostly derive. The elicited model is derived from captures by a pure fold (ADR-0003), all interpretation happens at write time as contestable captures, and model gaps mechanically cue grounded follow-up candidates. Interviewing strategy decides whether to ask, propose a likely structure for correction, or leave a visible gap. The spec is desk-validated on the baseline transcripts and cross-plugin thumbnails (Gherkin, formal verification, CPS); its ratification condition is a full worked pass across three plugin targets, and its open questions are carried as first-class sections with owning tickets rather than folded into the design.
issues.proposedTitle: Define declarative plugin authoring
issues.proposedOuter: New elicitation domains currently require bespoke engineering, and the system lacks a declared path from source-traceable captures to a useful domain model and completion judgment. The provisional plugin contract reduces authoring to two schemas and two small tables, with interpretation recorded when captures are written and model views derived later. Ratification still requires a full worked pass across three plugin targets, and named tickets own the remaining questions.

The 2026-08-18 integration meeting settled the September demo's staging: the elicitor is presented inside [demo.petrinaut.org](<http://demo.petrinaut.org>)'s existing chat panel, not in a separate demo application. FE-1448 adds the generic host component mechanism; FE-1449 is the durable, visibly inspectable prototype that proves the actual brunch ask suspends and resumes without laundering provenance.

issues.proposedTitle: Test whether Flue resumes batched client-tool results
issues.proposedOuter: Determine whether Flue can end a turn with pending client tools and later resume the same session with batched outputs recorded as non-user entries. The verdict will shape both the external-tool protocol and FE-1395’s questionnaire chaining. If Flue cannot carry this form, select the document-handle fallback for the demo and record evidence for a second binding.
issues.innerRecord:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## Question

Can Flue end a turn with client-tool calls pending and resume on a later dispatch — per-session state intact, the batched outputs re-entering the loop as machine entries? This is the first of the spec's two gating spikes: the external-tool round-trip is designed to ride the same suspension floor as the ask protocol (one substrate capability, two core protocols), and that only holds if the substrate carries the shape.

The verdict feeds two consumers: the external-tool round-trip protocol ticket (this graph) and FE-1395's questionnaire chaining, which stands on the same pending-slot batching ground. Failure here is not failure of the harness: it selects the spec's doc-handle fallback for the demo and files as evidence toward a `binding-pi`.

Spec: integration spec (FE-1433) testing decisions; kernel spec §7.3/§7.4 (suspension, one live affordance), §9.4 (provenance discrimination), §10 (binding capabilities).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A written verdict records whether terminate-with-pending plus resume-on-dispatch holds, referencing the probe code or transcript
- [ ] The verdict states whether batched outputs (several tool results in one dispatch) bind cleanly, and adjudicates batch-as-pending-slot-variant vs. a parallel channel — or names exactly what remains undecided for the protocol ticket
- [ ] Returned tool outputs demonstrably enter as non-user entries (never anchorable as evidence)
- [ ] Observed round-trip counts are noted against the tool-call-per-element scaling concern (survey §6d: a 40-place net is ~100 mutations)
- [ ] On failure: the doc-handle fallback is selected in writing and the evidence filed toward a second binding

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately. The spike is throwaway; only the verdict persists.

issues.sourceTitle: The elicitor builds and repairs the net through Petrinaut's client-executed tools
issues.proposedTitle: Build and repair Petrinaut nets through client tools
issues.proposedOuter: Answers in the elicitor must create and change the net on Petrinaut’s canvas through Petrinaut’s existing client-executed tools. Add an external-tool round-trip protocol beside the question protocol, generate tool definitions from Petrinaut’s exported schemas, and keep returned outputs mechanically excluded from user evidence. FE-1434 determines the batching shape, and this work must coordinate with FE-1395 because both change the same pending-response rules.
issues.innerRecord:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

The demo's central beat: answering the elicitor's questions makes the net appear and change on the Petrinaut canvas. The elicitor drives the panel's existing client-executed tool surface — the panel runs known tools against the live editor and posts the outputs back — via a new **external-tool round-trip protocol** in `core`, sitting beside the ask protocol on the same suspension floor and shaped by the suspension spike's verdict (FE-1434) on batch-vs-pending-slot.

The elicitor's Petrinaut tools are generated from `petrinaut-core`'s exported tool schemas, so the tool surface tracks Petrinaut's own contract rather than a hand-copied one. Provenance is a hard invariant: returned tool outputs enter as machine entries, mechanically excluded from evidence-span anchoring (§9.4) — capture spans only ever cite the user. Retries and duplicate dispatches are idempotent per the affordance-protocol guarantees FE-1420 establishes.

**Coordination note (soft, deliberate):** FE-1395's questionnaire chaining stands on the same pending-slot batching ground. Either may land first, but not concurrently by different agents — whichever lands first writes the §7.3/§7.4 amendment; the other consumes it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Answering in the panel produces net mutations on the canvas through client-executed tools, and the elicitor sees TypeScript diagnostics after code-writing mutations
- [ ] The round-trip protocol lives in `core`, tested substrate-free at the ask-protocol seam (FE-1422's extraction is the prior art)
- [ ] Tool schemas are generated from `petrinaut-core`'s contract, not hand-copied
- [ ] Returned tool outputs are machine entries: citing one as evidence is mechanically refused, red-proved
- [ ] A duplicate dispatch of the same tool outputs does not double-apply
- [ ] The §7.3/§7.4 amendment has landed — here or already via FE-1395, per the coordination rule

## Blocked by

* FE-1434 (suspension spike — the batch-binding verdict shapes the protocol)
* FE-1436 (conversation slice — the wire path this rides on)
* FE-1422 (ask protocol in core — the protocol home this extends)
* Coordinate with (not blocked by): FE-1395

issues.sourceTitle: Elicitation sessions are private per browser and survive a reload
issues.proposedTitle: Keep elicitation sessions private and durable per browser
issues.proposedOuter: An elicitation must survive a reload while remaining inaccessible to another browser. The demo site will send a random browser identifier, the server will resolve it to sessions, and storage will enforce an opaque owner key without adding principals to the harness core. This identification is sufficient for the accepted demo threat model, while deployment separately owns rate limits and the origin allowlist.
issues.innerRecord:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

A visitor's elicitation is theirs: it survives a page reload, and another browser cannot see or alter it. The demo site mints a random UID into localStorage and sends it on every transport request; the host-authored server layer resolves principal → session set; the harness stays principal-free (session-id keyed). The storage port gains an **opaque owner key**, stamped at session creation — cross-principal access fails as a store-level refusal, the port's existing enforcement idiom, red-proved per the FE-1419 discipline.

The principal is deliberately ui-shell-owned (spec §4) so HASH's Ory identity can replace the localStorage UID later without touching the harness. The UID is identification, not authentication — the demo threat model accepts this; the front-door mitigations (rate limiting, origin allowlist) are the deployment ticket's. This ticket implements the auth/per-conversation-authorization gate of FE-1423 for the elicitor server. The kernel spec §9.6 owner-key amendment lands here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reloading the page resumes the same session and transcript; a different browser profile cannot read or write it
- [ ] The owner key is opaque to the binding; cross-principal refusals are proved red-first at the store seam
- [ ] The harness remains principal-free — no principal type appears in `core`
- [ ] Spec §9.6 gains the owner-key amendment in the same change
- [ ] FE-1423's auth gate is checked off with a pointer here

## Blocked by

* FE-1436 (conversation slice — the server and wire path this scopes)

issues.innerRecord:
## Parent

The elicitor server runs on HASH infrastructure — owned jointly with infra, who confirmed Postgres exists and deployment is unblocked once the code lives in `hashintel/hash`. ## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

Petrinaut hosts can supply custom interactive chat-tool components through the public `aiAssistant` configuration. Today the panel has the right internal pattern — an interactive-tool definition with input parsing, a widget, awaiting/submitted state, and `addToolOutput` submission — but its registry is private and hard-coded to Petrinaut's own `applyAutoLayout` tool. Unknown dynamic tools are rejected before a host can render or handle them.

Add a generic, typed host extension in `@hashintel/petrinaut` and prove it with a synthetic host tool in tests and a visible story or equivalent runnable surface. - [ ] Existing Petrinaut interactive and mutation tools are unchanged, and an unregistered dynamic tool still fails loudly
- [ ] The public type/API and lifecycle are documented and proved by focused tests plus a visible story or equivalent runnable example

- [ ] The implementation is committed on an isolated `hashintel/hash` branch; no temporary monkey-patch or browser shim is part of the proof

issues.sourceTitle: A structured brunch question suspends and resumes visibly in Petrinaut
issues.proposedTitle: Prove a structured brunch question suspends and resumes in Petrinaut
issues.proposedOuter: The next working prototype must connect the actual brunch agent to Petrinaut’s chat panel through the existing structured question flow. A correlated human answer must resume the same Flue conversation, while stale, forged, duplicate, unrelated, and machine-generated outputs remain excluded from user evidence. The committed prototype must also make question state, correlation IDs, suspension, return, and resumption visible without feeding diagnostics into evidence.
issues.innerRecord:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

The next working prototype pulls the proven seams together and remains as the base for later demo work. In Petrinaut's real panel, the actual brunch agent invokes its existing structured `brunch_ask` affordance; a host-supplied component renders the current free-text form; submitting it resumes the suspended Flue conversation through `transport-aisdk`; and the next agent turn appears in the same panel.

This slice must settle provenance at the wire boundary. A human response submitted by the registered ask component travels in an AI SDK tool-output-shaped message, but it is not a machine tool result. Only a response matching the currently pending brunch ask and its stable tool-call id may be projected into the harness's user-affordance reply path; stale, forged, duplicate, or unrelated tool outputs must not become user evidence. Petrinaut mutation outputs remain non-user machine entries. FE-1395 will extend the form catalog later without replacing this transport distinction.

The prototype is deliberately legible: normal chat renders reasoning and text, the custom ask component renders its structured question and awaiting/submitted state, and an opt-in inspector or diagnostic surface shows request/turn boundaries, part kinds, correlation ids, suspension, return, and resumption. This observability is committed and tested, while remaining structurally excluded from evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The actual agent invokes `brunch_ask`; Petrinaut renders it through the host component; one submitted answer resumes the same Flue conversation and produces the next visible agent turn
- [ ] The current free-text affordance envelope and markdown floor are consumed without inventing the choice/questionnaire schemas owned by FE-1395
- [ ] Only the currently pending ask's correlated human submission becomes a user-affordance reply and may be cited as evidence; stale, forged, duplicate, and non-ask tool outputs fail or remain non-user
- [ ] Awaiting → submitted → resumed state and stable ids are visibly inspectable alongside the normal panel output
- [ ] The runnable integration, component registration, server path, and automated proof remain committed; the prototype requires no fetch shim or disposable harness
- [ ] Contract tests cover the translated ask part and return POST; a real-panel test or runnable story proves the custom component lifecycle

## Blocked by

* FE-1436 (durable real-panel transport and server path)
* FE-1448 (generic host-supplied interactive tool components in Petrinaut)
* FE-1422 (portable ask protocol in core)
* FE-1434 (suspension and machine-result provenance verdict)

## Coordination

FE-1395 owns the later form catalog and reserved structured-tap encoding. This slice proves the transport-level distinction and current free-text form only; FE-1395 consumes it rather than designing a second component mechanism.
